title: Strict Roos cone comparison with total derived inverse limit and evaluations
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site and $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and put $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Assume countable products in $\mathcal A$ are exact. Write $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\ge1}^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal A)$ for the category of strict towers [def-weil-inverse-system]. Let $X_\bullet$ be any integer cochain complex of strict towers, with transitions $t_n:X_{n+1}\to X_n$, and let $u:X_\bullet\to I_\bullet$ be a K-injective resolution in $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)$, meaning a quasi-isomorphism to a complex $I_\bullet$ such that every chain map from an acyclic complex of towers to $I_\bullet$ is chain homotopic to zero. Derived categories and quasi-isomorphisms are as in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Set $P_X=\prod_n X_n$ termwise and $s_X:P_X\to P_X$ by $\mathrm{pr}_n s_X=t_n\mathrm{pr}_{n+1}$ [def-weil-tower-transition-endomorphism], and put $\operatorname{Roos}(X)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s_X)[-1]$ with differential $(y,x)\mapsto(-d y-(1-s_X)x,d x)$. Define $\operatorname{Roos}(I)$ in the same way, and $L_I=\lim_n I_n$ termwise, which represents the total right derived inverse limit of $X_\bullet$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Both arrows in the zigzag
$$\operatorname{Roos}(X)\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Roos}(u)}\operatorname{Roos}(I)\xleftarrow{\eta}L_I$$
are quasi-isomorphisms, where $\operatorname{Roos}(u)$ applies $\prod_nu_n$ to both cone coordinates and $\eta(z)=(0,z)$. For each $n$, the resulting isomorphism $\theta:\operatorname{Roos}(X)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim X_\bullet$ in $D(\mathcal A)$ is compatible with evaluation: $e_n\theta$ equals the chain projection $\operatorname{Roos}(X)\to X_n$, $(y,x)\mapsto\mathrm{pr}_n x$, in $D(\mathcal A)$, where $e_n:R\lim X_\bullet\to X_n$ is represented by $L_I\to I_n$ followed by $u_n^{-1}$ in $D(\mathcal A)$.

source.place: Tag 07KC, lemma-products, and Tag 08TC, definition-derived-limit. The evaluation-preserving zigzag for an arbitrary strict tower is the agent-written comparison with the K-injective Roos model, as needed by the last paragraph of def-weil-rationalization-karoubi.

proof.text: Use the canonical natural isomorphism between the limit of evaluated tower complexes and the complex obtained by applying lim termwise. Whisker it with localization and transport the right-derived-functor unit supplied by ringedStrictTowerHomotopyLimitOfUniverses. Apply strictRoosComparison to obtain its cone functor F, canonical coordinates, evaluations and augmentation normalization.

Module sheaves are Grothendieck with independent universes by lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck. Exact filtered colimits in the tower functor category are levelwise; a separator is supplied by the free-Yoneda generator of the presheaf category. Resolve I by the existing degreewise-injective K-injective replacement v:I→K. The K-injective quasi-isomorphism v is a homotopy equivalence. Applying the additive lim functor and transporting along the natural limit isomorphism proves that lim(v) is a quasi-isomorphism.

Apply the augmentation clause of strictRoosComparison to the compatible limit projections of I and the resolution v. It gives b:lim I→F(I) with coordinates (0,z), lam:lim I→lim K equal to lim(v), and Q(b)κ_Iρ_I=Q(lam)d_K. The right side and κ_Iρ_I are invertible, so b is a quasi-isomorphism. Functorial descent similarly makes F(u) a quasi-isomorphism. Transport F(u), b and a_X along the object equality F(T)=Roos(T), retaining all coordinate equations.

Define a_I by the same canonical second-coordinate projection. In each degree the equations for products and biproducts imply η a_I=π_I and Roos(u)a_I=a_X u_n. Exact evaluation gives QuasiIso u_n. Set ε=asIso(Qη), θ=asIso(Qρ) ε inverse and υ=asIso(Qu_n). Apply Q to the two chain equations and cancel ε and υ to obtain the asserted evaluation identity for the actual zigzag.

proof_origin.note: Lean proof from existing comparison and augmentation normalization, with canonical termwise-limit transport and K-injective homotopy invariance.
